Contract.title: A fourth skill, grace5-orchestrate, runs several approved changes in one mostly unattended session, and every skill reads a repository's optional local extensions
Contract.Problem: Explicit owner requirement of 2026-11-13: GRACE 5 must ship, out of the box, the counterpart of the GRACE 4 batch orchestrator, which was bound to GRACE 4 and to one project and cannot be reused. Today the three skills carry one change each; running several in a row, unattended, with the owner asked only what is critical, is left to each session's improvisation; the revision 3 approval brief also has malformed head metadata and requires a corrected approval surface without changing implementation, scope or check definitions. The closed change C-0009 later edited models/architecture/schemas/approval.xsd inside its own boundary, and that authorized edit necessarily enters this change's complete diff, so the Protected boundary must narrow to the schema files this change itself must not write, again changing no implementation, scope or check definition. A repository also has no place to tell every GRACE 5 role once how it works locally, for example which issue tracker receives discoveries or how an implementer is launched.
Contract.Change: Local extensions. A repository may keep prose instruction files in .grace5/extensions/, one topic per file, each saying in its own words which roles it addresses. The folder is optional; the kernel never creates, reads, writes or validates it. Each of the four skills says, in one sentence, that its reader reads the files there before working and follows those addressed to its role, and method.md defines the folder in one section. An extension may replace a skill's default and may grant standing authority for outward-facing actions; it cannot grant, and no skill takes from it, an owner gate the kernel reserves. The orchestrated run. A fourth skill, skills/grace5-orchestrate, defines it. One orchestrating session takes the open changes that status reports as approved for execution, lists every other open change as left out with the reason, and carries each taken change from start to close through subagents: an implementer that follows grace5-execute and an independent reviewer that follows grace5-review. The orchestrator implements nothing itself, reads the state of a change from grace5 status and never from a subagent's report, runs grace5 close, and keeps a run ledger on disk from which a fresh session can resume. By default changes run one at a time in the current worktree, in id order, each closed or parked before the next starts; concurrency and isolated workspaces exist only where an extension provides and authorizes them. The owner is asked only about a critical stop, and the skill lists the classes: an owner gate the kernel reserves (approval of a material revision, a manual observation, an owner-disposed finding); uncommitted work, not made by the run, found inside a change's Affected paths; an outward-facing or irreversible action without standing authority (a push, a deploy, creating a branch or a worktree); a failed required check or a blocking finding that remains after two fix rounds, a fix round being one return of the change to its implementer to correct the product inside the contract; an extension may set another number and may add classes. A change at a critical stop is parked in the ledger with its question and the run continues with every later change that does not depend on it, a change depending on a parked one when its contract names it or when the orchestrator reads a path common to both Affected lists, in which case it is parked too as waiting; the owner receives all parked questions in one round when nothing else can move. Every other decision is the orchestrator's and is written to the ledger. Run ledgers live under .grace5/orchestration/runs/ and are committed when the run ends. Delivery. The 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 migration step installs grace5-orchestrate in every skill location that already holds a packaged skill, and nowhere else, and refreshes the three installed skills. The packaged name joins the kernel-managed skill directories of source-identity.md. The existing 0.6.0 version and pin are retained; no release, tag update or machine-wide installation is part of this change. Standing isolation rules distinguish standalone execution from this serial batch, retaining each parked change's complete diff, evidence invalidation and Protected boundaries; outstanding pending or running dispatches are reconciled and canceled before a run is reported finished. Decision statements in contracts and briefs use neutral language without conversational attribution or direct speech. Difference briefs follow a framework authoring rule: one legend and color plus symbols distinguish added, modified and removed items, while unmodified items remain visually normal without repeated status labels.

Constraints.Constraint: No approval, execution authorization or owner disposition is set or inferred by the orchestrator, a subagent or an extension; a standing instruction to run changes unattended is none of these.

The run writes no kernel record by hand and adopts no pre-existing work. .grace5/extensions/ and .grace5/orchestration/ are in the state directory, so writing an extension or a ledger changes no candidate.
The migration step is idempotent, self-verifying, declares that it touches no change, and writes only kernel-managed paths.

L-24 is added for the skill and extensions folder, with its removal criterion. Existing L-07 is amended to distinguish standalone isolation from the approved serial batch: later authorized changes can appear in a parked change's complete diff, so the worktree is no longer claimed to make that diff belong to only one change. Existing L-04 also records neutral decision statements, the visual difference-brief convention and its removal criterion.

The surface grows by one skill, one migration step and two directories in the state that the kernel never writes, .grace5/extensions/ for the owner's instructions and .grace5/orchestration/ for the orchestrator's ledgers, and by nothing else: no command, schema, record kind, topic document or validation is added, and no skill or document names a product, tracker, container runtime or harness-specific tool as required.

grace5-orchestrate cites the three lifecycle skills and the method documents and does not restate them. Each lifecycle skill gains the one sentence on extensions; grace5-execute also amends its isolation instruction for standalone execution and the serial-batch exception, and grace5-prepare amends its Decision-authoring instruction to require neutral statements rather than attributed direct speech. The lifecycle skills are otherwise unchanged. method.md, source-identity.md and L-07 state the same isolation exception: one active implementer, parked changes permitted, each original start revision retained, every later source commit included in the complete diff and invalidating earlier evidence, and no waiver of Protected paths or adoption of foreign work.

The required independent review evaluates A1 and A2 against the complete implementation diff and the recorded rehearsal specified in D9: its raw ledger, session report, commit log, kernel receipts and status, including contrary evidence and after-run interventions. It also judges A6 against the authoring rule, template and rendered current brief. The reviewer neither authored the implementation nor ran the rehearsal; a preparer's summary or a supporting audit alone is insufficient. Failed behavior is a blocking finding; missing evidence makes the review incomplete. CK4's association with A1 and A2 establishes package identity, not behavioral proof; CK3 does not prove visual fidelity. The owner has no log-reading or manual observation task for this change.

Decision text in contracts and briefs states policies and tradeoffs neutrally: no ambiguous speaker labels, conversational attribution/date prefixes or copied direct speech. Technical literals and named responsibilities remain explicit where they affect behavior; formal approval authority and provenance remain in approval records. Difference briefs use one compact legend, green plus markers for added items, amber tilde markers for modified items, and red minus markers for removed items; unmodified items use normal styling without repeated status labels. Meaning remains visible without color and in print. brief.md and grace5-prepare make this mandatory; templates/brief.html supplies neutral headings, its style and legend example. Current-revision fidelity entries remain present; removed historical items do not masquerade as current entries. Approved historical briefs and approval records are not rewritten. The current unapproved brief previews this convention; no kernel parser, schema or new validation mechanism is added.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Preparing, briefing or approving changes inside a run; a change not approved for execution is listed and left out.
Any kernel reading, schema, naming rule or validation of an extension file or a run ledger.
A shipped extension, or a shipped integration with an issue database, a container runtime or any other tool; those are written by each repository.
Overlap detection by the kernel, or a scheduler for concurrent changes; the deferred proposal of method.md stays deferred.
Installing the skill in a pilot repository or writing any pilot's extensions; each takes the version on the owner's explicit request.

Acceptance.Criterion: A fresh session given only the packaged skill carries an approved change to a kernel close without asking the owner anything, parks a change that reaches a critical stop with its question while the remaining changes proceed, commits its ledger, asks its parked questions in one round, infers no approval, and makes no push, branch or worktree; the independent review specified in K7 judges the rehearsal behavior.
One extension file addressed to every role is followed by the orchestrator and by its subagents alike in the rehearsal inspected by the independent reviewer specified in K7.

The 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 step installs grace5-orchestrate beside installed packaged skills in each location, creates no location, changes nothing when applied twice, and leaves every change's hashes and candidate as they were; a conformance case fails when the kernel lacks it.
The kernel type-checks, the examples still verify, the three packages carry the four skills, and neither they nor the CLI reference drift from their sources.
The kernel reports grace5 0.6.0 and this repository's pin reads 0.6.0.

The prepare skill, brief authoring rule and template require K8's neutral decision statements and visual difference convention. The current unapproved brief uses neutral decisions, one legend and correctly highlighted additions and modifications instead of repeated status labels. Independent review judges presentation and comparison with the previous approved revision; CK3 covers continued compatibility of the existing brief fidelity examples.

Automated.Command: bun -e "const fs = require('fs'); const out = require('child_process').execFileSync('bun', ['src/cli.ts', '--version']).toString().trim(); const pin = fs.existsSync('.grace5/kernel-version') ? fs.readFileSync('.grace5/kernel-version', 'utf8').trim() : ''; const skill = fs.existsSync('packages/skills/grace5-orchestrate/SKILL.md'); process.exit(out === 'grace5 0.6.0' && pin === '0.6.0' && skill ? 0 : 1)"

Decisions.Decision: GRACE 5 ships an orchestrator skill that manages subagents for open changes, works mostly autonomously, escalates only critical issues and supports local extensions. Issue databases and containerised implementers remain possible without a required product or integration.
A run takes only changes whose current revision is approved for execution and lists every other open change as left out with its reason.
Optional prose files in a well-known folder share repository-local instructions across roles. The kernel adds no schema or validation for them.
A change at a critical stop is parked while independent work continues. All parked questions are presented in one round when nothing else can move.

Local instructions live in .grace5/extensions/ and committed run ledgers in .grace5/orchestration/runs/. Both are outside the candidate: extension edits stale no evidence and are outside changes' reviewed source diffs. Ledgers are committed when the run ends.
The existing 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 migration installs the new skill beside packaged skills already present in a repository, rather than requiring a manual copy.
Without an extension, changes run one at a time in the current worktree.
The four critical classes are the minimum escalations. Extensions may add classes but cannot remove kernel owner gates.

An independent agent reviewer judges one recorded rehearsal in a scratch git repository outside this one, initialized by the candidate kernel with its four packaged skills. Four changes edit separate files, share no Affected path and name no dependency: the first has a required automated check that cannot pass inside its boundary; the second also has a fixture manual check naming the owner; the third can close; the fourth is unapproved. The fixture author writes approval records marked as fixtures; they approve nothing real. One extension, .grace5/extensions/commits.md, addresses every role and requires the trailer "Rehearsal: yes" on every run-made commit, granting no authority. A fresh session receives only the instruction to run open changes with grace5-orchestrate. Review establishes that the first two changes park with critical questions, the third kernel-closes before requests for owner answers, the fourth is excluded, questions are presented together, every run-made commit has the trailer, the ledger is committed, no branch/worktree/push or approval change occurred, and the orchestrator wrote no Affected product file. No owner observation is required for this change, and an agent is never recorded as a human observer. Reviewers state the limits of this single rehearsal.

This change creates no release. The existing version 0.6.0, pin and v0.6.0 tag are retained. Framework version creation and machine installation require an explicit owner request. Scratch skill copies stay within the rehearsal fixture. Execution uses master without a branch.
The required independent agent review assesses the rehearsal and implementation and reports concise findings. The owner has no log-reading or manual observation task.

Resolve F1 by aligning the executor and standing isolation rules: standalone execution retains one change per worktree; serial batches may retain parked changes with one active implementer. Original start revisions, complete diffs, stale-evidence rules and Protected boundaries remain. No source filtering or concurrent scheduler is added. Resolve F2 by reconciling and canceling outstanding pending or running dispatches before reporting completion.

Contracts and briefs use neutral decision statements without conversational ownership labels or attributed direct speech. Difference briefs use one legend and color plus symbols for additions, modifications and removals, with normal styling for unmodified items. Approved historical brief and approval-record bytes are preserved. Formal approval authority and provenance remain in approval records; this draft change does not approve the pending isolation or dispatch fixes.
